why: Counting LRU page faults is an LRU cache in disguise: a hash map from page to node and a doubly linked list in recency order give O(1) hit checks, move-to-most-recent and eviction of the least recent page. The OA story only changes what you report (the faults).
hints: For each access you must know: is the page cached, and which cached page was used longest ago?
A hash map answers the first in O(1). A doubly linked list ordered by recency answers the second: the least recent page is at one end, and a hit moves its node to the other end in O(1).
On a hit, unlink the node and append it at the most-recent end. On a miss, count a fault; if full, remove the least-recent node and its map entry; then append the new page.
pitfalls: Capacity 0 stores nothing: every access is a fault.
A hit must refresh the page's recency, not only count as a hit.
